newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dutch say accept Britain will not lift borders.
newsitem.headline: Dutch say accept Britain will not lift borders.

text.p: The chairman of the main inter-governmental conference (IGC) negotiating group said on Tuesday he accepted that no British government would lift passport controls and that London's EU partners would have to go it alone.

Dutch European Affairs Minister Michiel Patijn told a news conference it was a "political fact" that neither the current British government nor a future one would budge on the issue of border controls.

The result was that a flexible approach was needed that would allow other EU countries to create a border-free Union without Britain or Ireland, the two EU countries that have not signed up up to the Schengen Agreement.

The Netherlands, the EU presidency, proposed on Monday that the agreement, which lifts passport controls among members and shares police data, be brought into the European Union treaty when a new one is agreed later this year.
It said that representatives from London and Dublin would be allowed to sit in on discussions but not to take part.
Conversely, officials from Norway and Iceland, two non-EU member that have cooperation pacts with Schengen countries, could be given an active role.

Patijn, who emphasised he was speaking personally, said he saw no reason if Schengen was part of the EU why Britain and Ireland could not participate in the sharing of police data without lifting their border controls.
